claims.explanation: Thiocolchicoside is a colchicoside-derived tubulin-binding agent that kills cancer cells through microtubule destabilization and NF-κB pathway inhibition, with apoptosis via Bcl-2/XIAP downregulation. Selective sensitivity is best explained by intact apoptotic signaling and dependence on NF-κB-driven survival, while protective features include mutations that activate alternative survival or differentiation programs (e.g., CTNNB1, SF3B1, EGFR) and low expression of drug transporters or GABA/glycine receptor subunits that may mediate off-target uptake.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive list, consistent with impaired DNA damage/apoptosis checkpoints enhancing microtubule-poison killing
High NF-κB activity supports survival; thiocolchicoside downregulates NF-κB and its antiapoptotic targets
Thiocolchicoside suppresses Bcl-2; high Bcl-2 expression blunts apoptosis
XIAP is an NF-κB-regulated survival factor downregulated by thiocolchicoside
CTNNB1-mutant lines (KE39, HEC265) are among least affected, suggesting Wnt/β-catenin survival signaling
SF3B1-mutant lines (UO31, HCC95) are least affected, possibly via altered splicing of apoptotic regulators
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, NCIH1648, KYSE270) are least affected, suggesting RTK-driven survival
Thiocolchicoside antagonizes GABAA receptors; expression may mediate non-tubulin effects or uptake
Thiocolchicoside interacts with strychnine-sensitive glycine receptors; expression may contribute to sensitivity
BRAF-mutant melanomas appear in sensitive list, though BRAF-mutant lines also appear in resistant list, so weak
KRAS-mutant lines (CL11, SNU410) are among least affected, suggesting MAPK-driven survival
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines (FTC133, 786O, UACC62), consistent with PI3K/AKT dependence on NF-κB survival
